Break the import from:

`src/domain/billing.ts` → `src/presentation/invoice-view.ts`

Why: it is both an edge in the three-file cycle and a confirmed architecture violation—domain code should not depend on presentation code. Removing it restores the intended dependency direction and breaks the runtime cycle:

`billing-flow → billing → invoice-view → billing-flow`

Move any shared types or formatting-neutral data structures into a leaf module such as `src/domain/invoice.ts` or `src/contracts/invoice.ts`, then let both layers import from there. If the domain import is used only for TypeScript types, converting it to `import type` may be sufficient; otherwise, inject a domain-owned interface or move presentation-specific behavior into `invoice-view.ts`.
